title: 'Superman': Warwick man remembered after bike accident - NewsBreak
text: NORTH KINGSTOWN, R.I. (WPRI) — Robert “Bob” Lamothe is being remembered by his friends as an impressive athlete who was larger than life. Michael Lynch and Fred Bartlett have each known Lamothe for decades. “There was nobody like him,” Bartlett told 12 News on Wednesday. “He went full bore all the time. No rest days, no days off.” “We are fortunate to have been his friends,” Lynch added. Every Saturday, Lamothe would ride his bike on a route that traveled through North Kingstown. Police said that this Saturday, Lamothe was in a crash at the intersection of Essex and Potter roads. Emergency crews found him unresponsive, and he later died at the hospital. “He was this idol, this superman,” Bartlett said. “The fact that he was out riding, and passed away at only 71 years old, for all this training and all the things we do health wise… you should be 80s, 90s, 100s.” Lamothe spent 30 years teaching special education at North Providence High School. He was also a coach and referee at the Rhode Island Interscholastic League. According to his friends, Lamothe was an intense athlete, he was also kind and caring. “We had two rules to follow. Rule one, surround yourself with good friends. Rule two, never forget rule one,” Lynch said. “Bob never forgot rule one. He was always there through thick and thin.” Lamothe’s friends said despite the shock of his death, they are comforted knowing he died doing what he loved. “I know that, deep down, he did exactly what he said he was going to do,” Bartlett said. “He’s going to rest when he dies.” Lamothe’s funeral services are scheduled for this Saturday.
